bindings.absent_bindings_reason: This model proves grammar, duality and endpoint-resource theorems over a handwritten closed definitions table. No lowering helper, runtime or peer is a subject of these theorems, so binding one would imply a correspondence this package does not establish. WIT-SESSION-06 stays open.

theorems.name: NestedSession.dual_is_involutive
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: duality is definitional and involutive on every node
theorems.statement: NestedSession.dual_is_involutive : ∀ (node : NestedSession.Node), NestedSession.dual (NestedSession.dual node) = node

theorems.name: NestedSession.dual_swaps_send_and_recv
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: duality swaps Send/Recv on the same ordered message type
theorems.statement: NestedSession.dual_swaps_send_and_recv : ∀ (message : NestedSession.MessageType) (continuation : Nat), NestedSession.dual (NestedSession.Node.send message continuation) = NestedSession.Node.recv message continuation

theorems.name: NestedSession.dual_swaps_choose_and_offer
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: internal choice duals to external choice on the same branch
theorems.statement: NestedSession.dual_swaps_choose_and_offer : ∀ (branch continuation : Nat), NestedSession.dual (NestedSession.Node.choose branch continuation) = NestedSession.Node.offer branch continuation

theorems.name: NestedSession.resolve_refuses_exhaustion
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: bounded unfolding refuses a nested constructor at depth zero instead of accepting it
theorems.statement: NestedSession.resolve_refuses_exhaustion : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (index name parameter : Nat), definitions[index]? = some (NestedSession.Node.nested name parameter) → NestedSession.resolve definitions 0 index = none

theorems.name: NestedSession.resolve_unfolds_with_depth
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: a nested constructor resolves to its named definition rather than expanding without bound
theorems.statement: NestedSession.resolve_unfolds_with_depth : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (index name parameter : Nat), definitions[index]? = some (NestedSession.Node.nested name parameter) → NestedSession.resolve definitions 1 index = definitions[name]?

theorems.name: NestedSession.resolve_refuses_unknown_definition
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-01: an index outside the closed table is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.resolve_refuses_unknown_definition : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (depth : Nat), NestedSession.resolve definitions depth definitions.length = none

theorems.name: NestedSession.send_step_does_not_observe_a_peer
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03: a send step observes no peer; receipt is not modelled
theorems.statement: NestedSession.send_step_does_not_observe_a_peer : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (depth : Nat) (endpoint successor : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.stepSend definitions depth endpoint = some successor → successor.responder = endpoint.responder ∧ successor.channel = endpoint.channel

theorems.name: NestedSession.endpoint_copy_is_refused
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: endpoint copy is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.endpoint_copy_is_refused : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.copy endpoint = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedCopy

theorems.name: NestedSession.endpoint_discard_is_refused
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: endpoint discard is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.endpoint_discard_is_refused : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.discard endpoint = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedDiscard

theorems.name: NestedSession.endpoint_capture_is_refused
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: endpoint capture is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.endpoint_capture_is_refused : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.capture endpoint = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedCapture

theorems.name: NestedSession.stale_generation_is_refused
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: identity alone does not authorise an operation
theorems.statement: NestedSession.stale_generation_is_refused : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.useWith endpoint endpoint.generation.succ = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedStale

theorems.name: NestedSession.matching_generation_is_accepted
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: the control keeping the refusal non-vacuous
theorems.statement: NestedSession.matching_generation_is_accepted : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.useWith endpoint endpoint.generation = NestedSession.Outcome.accepted

theorems.name: NestedSession.double_close_is_refused
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02: a second close is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.double_close_is_refused : ∀ (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint), NestedSession.closeOnce { channel := endpoint.channel, responder := endpoint.responder, protocol := endpoint.protocol, state := endpoint.state, generation := endpoint.generation, closed := true } = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedDoubleClose

theorems.name: NestedSession.closed_endpoint_cannot_send
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-02/03: a closed endpoint cannot send
theorems.statement: NestedSession.closed_endpoint_cannot_send : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (depth : Nat) (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint) (message : NestedSession.MessageType) (continuation : Nat), NestedSession.resolve definitions depth endpoint.state = some (NestedSession.Node.send message continuation) → NestedSession.stepSend definitions depth { channel := endpoint.channel, responder := endpoint.responder, protocol := endpoint.protocol, state := endpoint.state, generation := endpoint.generation, closed := true } = none

theorems.name: NestedSession.send_step_advances_to_the_continuation
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-04: one step advances exactly to the continuation and nothing outside the protocol
theorems.statement: NestedSession.send_step_advances_to_the_continuation : ∀ (definitions : List NestedSession.Node) (depth : Nat) (endpoint : NestedSession.Endpoint) (message : NestedSession.MessageType) (continuation : Nat), NestedSession.resolve definitions depth endpoint.state = some (NestedSession.Node.send message continuation) → NestedSession.stepSend definitions depth { channel := endpoint.channel, responder := endpoint.responder, protocol := endpoint.protocol, state := endpoint.state, generation := endpoint.generation, closed := false } = some { channel := endpoint.channel, responder := endpoint.responder, protocol := endpoint.protocol, state := continuation, generation := endpoint.generation, closed := false }

theorems.name: NestedSession.admitOne_is_bounded
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03: admission keeps the mailbox depth inside the limit, given a well-formed session
theorems.statement: NestedSession.admitOne_is_bounded : ∀ (queued limit : Nat), queued ≤ limit → NestedSession.admitOne queued limit ≤ limit

theorems.name: NestedSession.admission_is_bounded
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03: a session admission never exceeds the declared queue limit
theorems.statement: NestedSession.admission_is_bounded : ∀ (session : NestedSession.Session), session.queued ≤ session.queueLimit → (NestedSession.deliver session).queued ≤ session.queueLimit

theorems.name: NestedSession.full_mailbox_is_unchanged
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03: a full mailbox refuses by leaving the session unchanged, never a silent drop
theorems.statement: NestedSession.full_mailbox_is_unchanged : ∀ (session : NestedSession.Session), session.queueLimit ≤ session.queued → NestedSession.deliver session = session

theorems.name: NestedSession.admission_preserves_the_endpoint_inventory
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-05: admission copies and removes no endpoint
theorems.statement: NestedSession.admission_preserves_the_endpoint_inventory : ∀ (session : NestedSession.Session), (NestedSession.deliver session).endpoints = session.endpoints

theorems.name: NestedSession.no_endpoint_duplication
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-05: no operation in this model increases the endpoint inventory
theorems.statement: NestedSession.no_endpoint_duplication : ∀ (session : NestedSession.Session), (NestedSession.deliver session).endpoints.length ≤ session.endpoints.length

theorems.name: NestedSession.trace_send_then_recv
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03 positive trace: sequenced send advances the state and observes no peer
theorems.statement: NestedSession.trace_send_then_recv : Option.map (fun endpoint => endpoint.state) (NestedSession.stepSend NestedSession.exampleProtocol 2 { channel := 5, responder := false, protocol := 9, state := 0, generation := 4, closed := false }) = some 1

theorems.name: NestedSession.trace_recursive_entry_unfolds_to_the_send_node
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03 positive trace: recursive entry unfolds to the declared definition instead of expanding
theorems.statement: NestedSession.trace_recursive_entry_unfolds_to_the_send_node : NestedSession.resolve NestedSession.exampleProtocol 2 2 = some (NestedSession.Node.send NestedSession.MessageType.i64 1)

theorems.name: NestedSession.trace_orderly_close
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03 positive trace: orderly close is accepted once and a second close is refused
theorems.statement: NestedSession.trace_orderly_close : NestedSession.closeOnce { channel := 5, responder := false, protocol := 9, state := 3, generation := 4, closed := false } = NestedSession.Outcome.accepted ∧ NestedSession.closeOnce { channel := 5, responder := false, protocol := 9, state := 3, generation := 4, closed := true } = NestedSession.Outcome.refusedDoubleClose

theorems.name: NestedSession.trace_bounded_buffering_refuses_the_third_payload
theorems.role: WIT-SESSION-03 positive trace: bounded buffering stops at the declared limit
theorems.statement: NestedSession.trace_bounded_buffering_refuses_the_third_payload : (NestedSession.deliver (NestedSession.deliver (NestedSession.deliver { endpoints := [], queued := 0, queueLimit := 2 }))).queued = 2

scope: .cairn/changes/nested-session-protocol WIT-SESSION-01/02 model: finite grammar, duality and the endpoint resource.
The definitions table is handwritten. No lowering, runtime, scheduler, queue or peer correspondence is claimed,
no progress statement is made, endpoint delegation is excluded and send is never modelled as receipt.
